full_caption: Ulric Jarrowmere, Appellant, v. Ottoline Dunmoor, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Ulric Jarrowmere and Ottoline Dunmoor own riparian tracts along the Sable Fork within Ashbourne County. The dispute concerns Ottoline Dunmoor's diversion of approximately 1,575 gallons per minute for irrigation of 1.4 acres.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The public trust doctrine reserves to the State title to the beds of navigable waters. Navigability for title purposes is determined by susceptibility to commercial navigation at the date of statehood.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: A use that wholly deprives a downstream riparian of water for domestic purposes is unreasonable as a matter of law, without regard to the economic value of the upstream use.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Groundwater in this State is governed by the rule of reasonable use, under which an overlying owner may withdraw for beneficial use on the overlying land but may not export off-tract to the injury of neighboring wells.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Under the riparian doctrine as modified in this State, each riparian owner is entitled to a reasonable use of the watercourse, measured against the correlative rights of other riparians.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Reasonableness is a question of fact informed by the purpose of the use, its economic and social value, the extent of the harm, the practicality of avoiding the harm, and the protection of existing investments.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Accretion belongs to the riparian owner; avulsion does not change the boundary. The 1992 channel shift, being sudden and perceptible, was avulsive and left the boundary at the former thread of the stream.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The 105 days of well failure experienced by Ulric Jarrowmere coincided with the operation of Ottoline Dunmoor's high-capacity irrigation well 16 feet from the shared aquifer boundary. Causation was established by drawdown modeling.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The injunction is modified to permit diversion not exceeding 275 gallons per minute between May and October, and is otherwise affirmed.

sections.heading: RIDER A — DIVERSION LIMITS AND SEASONAL SCHEDULE
sections.text: The Upper Owner may divert from the Sable Fork for irrigation not more than 1,575 gallons per minute, and not more than an aggregate of 780 acre-feet in any calendar year. Between May and October the permitted rate is reduced to 275 gallons per minute. No diversion is permitted whenever the gauged flow at the Ashbourne County station falls below the minimum bypass flow set out in Rider B.

sections.heading: RIDER B — MINIMUM BYPASS FLOW AND MEASUREMENT
sections.text: A minimum bypass flow sufficient to satisfy downstream domestic and stock-watering needs shall be maintained at all times. Each diverting party shall install and maintain a totalizing meter at the point of diversion, shall record readings weekly, and shall furnish records to any other riparian owner within 10 days of written request. Domestic use has priority over irrigation, and irrigation over industrial use, in every period of shortage.

sections.heading: RIDER C — GROUNDWATER AND WELL INTERFERENCE
sections.text: No high-capacity well shall be completed within 16 feet of an existing domestic well without a drawdown analysis furnished to the affected owner. If operation of a high-capacity well causes an existing domestic well to fail or its yield to fall below five gallons per minute, the operator shall, at its expense, deepen or replace the affected well or provide an equivalent permanent supply. Withdrawal for export off the overlying tract is prohibited where it injures a neighboring overlying user.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Severability
sections.text: If any provision of this instrument is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to render it enforceable, and if it cannot be so reformed it shall be severed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.
